recon.notes: Added 2026-10-18 at the owner’s request. Folsom Europe e.V. runs Berlin’s leather week (festivals.json: 2026-09-10 → 2026-09-13, category kink); the August 2026 hand-extraction of its programme already put the bear-relevant nights into the Berlin calendar (Woof Berlin ×4, BearDance at SO36, the street fair). The site is WordPress + Elementor with The Events Calendar installed, but the two are not the same calendar: the public programme lives in an EMS "Event Control" programme embedded by iframe on /program/, while the Tribe calendar is the volunteer-shift roster (85 shifts, all category "Volunteering", 2025 and 2026). So with /program/ configured the crawler reads an event-less page, adopts the Tribe REST door, finds it empty from mid-September to the next July or August, and while shifts are posted (the 2026 shifts were dated 2026-09-09 … 2026-09-14; creation dates in the feed start 2025-07) reads shifts that the bear check must drop. Leather, not bear, so alwaysBear is false; the promoter entry in data/promoters.json carries the site and the Instagram handle the page itself links (https://www.instagram.com/folsomeurope), with no bearAffinity claim.

coverage.basis: Two independent doors agree the host publishes zero upcoming events on 2026-10-18: the REST route’s default window (total 0, door 2) and the Tribe list view’s own empty state ("There are no upcoming events.", door 3); the configured /program/ page (door 1) carries no event text of its own at all. The archive read (door 4, two pages, total 85 reconciled with 50 + 35 rows) shows the calendar’s whole history is volunteer shifts — past listings are counted (85), not enumerated, and would be traps even when upcoming. The public programme (door 5) is a past edition on another host that the parser does not read.

traps.label: wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events → "Set-up Team – Pre-Fair-Day / Aufbau-Team – Aufbautag", "Security Gate – Martin-Luther-Str.", "Animal Farm Volunteer / Helfer:in Animal Farm", "Hang up Flags, Street Decoration and Banners" … (85 rows, every one category "Volunteering")
traps.why: The Tribe calendar on this host is the crew roster: dated, timed, placed rows that are work shifts for volunteers, not programming for the public. When the 2027 shifts are posted (summer) they will be upcoming rows in the door the crawler adopts and will look exactly like events — bilingual titles, a street address, a 2–5 hour slot. Nothing bear about any of them; the bear check is what stands between them and the deck.

expect.note: config.allowPastEvents is true for every parser, so the past shifts ARE read: the validation run 20261018-112822 followed the list view’s "past" link and took all 85 rows from that page’s JSON-LD (title, dates, bar, address, url; no image, no cost), kept every one as "future" (86 → 86), and the bear check then dropped 50 of the 51 distinct shifts and FLAGGED one — "Take Down Flags / Fahnen abhängen" (2025-09-01 10:00–12:00) — which survived as the run’s single final event. So "extracted" is the correct expectation for a shift; the bear check is the only gate, and it let one through as a flag. When the 2027 shifts are upcoming the same 80-odd rows will arrive through the REST door instead.

traps.why: The real programme, on a third-party host, embedded by iframe. The crawler does not follow iframes and the parser is not configured for ems.switchedapp.com, so no row from it can be read from here; the 17 server-rendered rows it does carry are the past 2026 Wednesday. Documented so nobody reads the page heading "FOLSOM EUROPE 2026 SCHEDULE" as a dated event or the empty page as a broken site.

traps.why: The Tribe list view’s positive empty-state signal, HTTP 200, agreed by the REST door. Never an event, never a fetch failure.

openQuestions.q: The programme door. Three ways to read Folsom Europe’s actual programme, none built: (a) a generic crawler rule that follows an iframe’s src from a configured page as a discovered page (affects every site with embeds — maps, videos, ticket widgets — so it needs its own gate); (b) configure https://ems.switchedapp.com/programme/folsomeurope as a parser url (a third-party host, server-rendered one day per read: the other days need JavaScript); (c) leave the parser on /program/ and keep the programme a once-a-year hand extraction, as in August 2026. Which?

One shift reached the final list: the bear check flagged rather than dropped "Take Down Flags / Fahnen abhängen" (2025-09-01) in run 20261018-112822 (0 bear, 1 flagged, 50 dropped), so a 2025 volunteer shift stands in the results as a flagged event with no bar, no image and the site root as its website. Flag-don’t-drop is the doctrine, so this is a deck card, not a calendar write — but it shows a staffing row can pass the only gate this source has.

The Tribe REST door on this host will fill with 2027 volunteer shifts next summer. Should the Tribe reader learn a generic rule for staffing categories (a row whose only category is "Volunteering" is not programming), or is the bear check enough? No rule was added: one site is not evidence of a convention.

Berlin bars: data/bars/berlin.json was created with Woof Berlin and SO36 (the venues the 2026 bear nights used, coordinates from the owner’s Berlin calendar records). Metropol / Mikropol (ADAM, Kake’s Sunday Service, Bearhood Monster Bash) and Lütze Bar were left out — add them?
